title: The Day of the Stubborn Mitten
skyStory: A thin waning crescent hangs over the snowbanks, packing its bags in Sagittarius like an archer who has misplaced every single arrow. It shrugs. It will find them next month. Mars, warming its hands by a woodstove somewhere in the cosmos, finds this deeply relatable. February tiptoes in wearing three scarves and announces it is only twenty-eight days long, as if that settles anything.

reading: One mitten will go missing this morning and you will search for it with the focus of a detective in a long coat. It is in the sleeve of the coat you are wearing. The Tiger checks everywhere except its own pockets. File that under lessons.

The rest of the day rewards finishing. You have a half-built thing waiting, maybe a shelf, maybe an email, maybe a plan with four browser tabs. The [[Knight of Wands]] says close three tabs and finish one shelf. When it is done, stand back and admire it out loud, even if the only witness is the kettle.
joel.mission: Finish one small thing you started last week and announce it to the room like a ship launch.
joel.omen: A single glove perched on a fence post. Someone out there is also looking for something, and you will help a stranger before dinner.
joel.stoneWhy: grounding for the great mitten hunt
joel.elementWhy: a month that starts in snowboots

reading: The Wood Rat wakes up already knowing which part of the day will be silly. Probably the meeting that could have been two sentences. Bring a pen you love and doodle a small mountain in the margin while everyone talks in circles.

Later, someone will ask your advice in the hallway, casually, as if it were nothing. It is not nothing. Your Life Path 11 hears the real question underneath the polite one. Answer that one instead, gently, and watch their shoulders drop about two inches. That is your work today, and it counts.
nancy.mission: Draw a tiny mountain somewhere unexpected today, like a sticky note on the fridge, and leave it for someone to discover.
nancy.omen: A crow carrying something shiny. It means a clever idea will land in your lap by Wednesday.

together.text: Each of you names one thing you will finish before February ends. Say it to each other, out loud or by message, then forget about it for a while. The month is short and sneaky, but so are you two.

title: The Moon Drops By Nancy's Mountain
skyStory: The waning crescent slips into Capricorn, Nancy's own sign, and knocks politely on the mountain door with a casserole of starlight. Saturn answers in slippers. Meanwhile, somewhere down on Earth, a groundhog is being asked to forecast the weather, and the moon finds this hilarious. It has been watching winter for four billion years and still cannot predict it.

reading: It is Groundhog Day, and you will feel like you have lived this morning before. Same coffee, same window, same snowbank that refuses to move. Shake it up. Take a different route, sit in a different chair, put your socks on in the opposite order. The Tiger hates a rut.

Around 1:40 pm a small task will come back that you thought was finished. Do not growl at it. Fix it with the cheerful air of someone who has nowhere else to be. The [[Six of Pentacles]] notices how gracefully you take a redo, and it is quietly giving you points.
joel.mission: Change one tiny morning habit today, like which hand holds your mug, and notice if the day feels newer.
joel.omen: A shadow on the snow shaped like a rabbit. Six more weeks of winter, but six more weeks of good ideas too.
joel.stoneWhy: sending warmth up to Capricorn

reading: The moon has come home to your sign, and it wants to sit at your kitchen table and hear a story. Any story. You are the storyteller, and today your hands will dance so much that someone across the room will start nodding along without hearing a word.

Saturn, your ruler, is in an unusually generous mood. It hands you a small block of quiet time around mid-afternoon. Use it for something only you would think of. The [[Six of Swords]] glides past in the corner of your eye, boat steady, oars resting. The crossing is going better than you think.
nancy.mission: Tell someone the story of your favourite winter morning, with full hand choreography.
nancy.omen: Your reflection in a dark window catching you mid-smile. The moon in your sign is approving of the plan.

together.text: Send each other one weather forecast today, completely made up and extremely specific. Snow shaped like question marks at 4 pm. Sunshine that smells faintly of cinnamon. Whoever predicts the silliest weather gets to be the official groundhog until next year.

title: The Day Saturn Labels Everything
skyStory: Still in Capricorn, the crescent thins to a sliver, and Saturn has gotten into the label maker. Everything in the sky now has a tidy tag. Orion: belt, do not lose. Big Dipper: handle side up. The moon has a label too. It says fading, but fabulous. Mars tries to peel one off and gets a stern look.

reading: Saturn is tidying, and it is looking pointedly at your desk. You know the pile. The one with the cable, the receipt, the note that says call about the thing. Give the pile ten minutes. Not an hour. Ten minutes, with a timer, like a game show.

After that, the cabin feels bigger. Ideas have somewhere to land. Around 4 pm you will get a flash of something good for a project you set aside in autumn. Write it down before the kettle boils. The Tiger thinks fastest when the den is clear.
joel.mission: Tidy one surface for exactly ten minutes with a timer, then stop even if it is not perfect.
joel.omen: A label that is peeling at one corner. It means a small rule in your life is ready to be rewritten.
joel.stoneWhy: calm water for a tidy mind

reading: This is your kind of sky. Order, patience, a little quiet ambition. The Wood Rat in you spots the one thing in the room that is out of place, and you get to decide whether to fix it or let it be charming.

Someone will praise your work today in a way that feels too big. You will want to wave it off. Do not. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] is standing nearby, reversed and fidgeting, reminding you that you do not have to earn every kind word twice. Say thank you. Then say nothing else. It is a whole sentence.
nancy.mission: When someone compliments you today, say only thank you and let the silence afterward do the rest.
nancy.omen: A neatly stacked pile of firewood. It means your effort is building something sturdier than you can see.
nancy.stoneWhy: layers of good work, stacked high

together.text: Pick one tiny item that has been nagging both of you, a forgotten reply or a loose button, and each deal with yours before sunset. Report back in one word. Saturn is grading on effort today, and it is a generous marker.

title: The Blank Page Under a Dark Moon
skyStory: The new moon arrives in Capricorn, barely a whisper of light at four percent, and the sky goes dark and velvet like a fresh notebook. Saturn slides it across the table and says write something good. Mars immediately wants to write ten things. The moon raises an invisible eyebrow. One wish, it says. Make it count.

reading: New moons are for beginnings, and you love a beginning maybe a little too much. You have ideas the way a woodstove has sparks. Tonight the [[Knight of Wands]] asks you to choose one spark and blow on it gently, not ten at once.

So pick. Write it on a scrap of paper, fold it twice, and put it somewhere you will see it every day this month. Under the onyx bracelet's usual resting spot works. As a communicator, you know the power of saying a thing plainly. Say it plainly to yourself.
joel.mission: Write one goal for February on a scrap of paper, fold it twice, and hide it where you will see it daily.
joel.omen: A spark that pops out of a fire or a candle. It means your chosen idea has heard you.
joel.stoneWhy: dark moon, dark stone, clear intention

reading: The new moon in your own sign is a rare little gift, like finding a note from your past self in a coat pocket. The note says keep going. It also says you were right about that thing. You know the thing.

Tonight, set a quiet intention about helping someone level up, because that is what you love. Maybe it is a person. Maybe it is yourself. Saturn approves of goals with real steps, so give yours three. Write them small. The shore is dark and still, and the water is listening.
nancy.mission: Write a three-step plan for one small goal and tuck it under your pillow like a tooth for the moon fairy.
nancy.omen: A star visible through the clouds for just a moment. It means your wish is already on its way.
nancy.stoneWhy: the shore holds the new moon

together.text: Share your new moon intentions with each other in exactly seven words each. No more, no less. Count them on your fingers. Seven words is enough to start a fire and climb a mountain, and the moon will remember both.

title: The Day of the Two Orange Shovels
skyStory: The moon has drifted into Aquarius, the sign of odd inventions and strange coincidences, and at one percent it is basically invisible and loving it. An invisible moon can get away with anything. Tonight it is rearranging the universe's furniture to make sure two friends notice the same peculiar thing on the same day. Aquarius cackles softly.

reading: You will see a bright orange snow shovel today, leaning somewhere it should not be. Maybe against a mailbox. Maybe on a porch with no snow. Take note. It is about to become very important, in a completely ridiculous way.

Otherwise the day is easygoing. People will ask you to explain something and you will do it so well that someone takes notes. Life Path 3 shines in this kind of light. Around 6 pm you will want to tell Nancy something odd. Do it. The universe has set this one up carefully.
joel.mission: Photograph the strangest object you see outside today and send it without any explanation.
joel.omen: An orange shovel in an odd spot. If you hear about another one before bedtime, don't even scream.
joel.stoneWhy: sharp eyes catch orange things

reading: The Wood Rat sees what others miss, and today that includes one very orange snow shovel abandoned in a place that makes zero sense. You will tilt your head at it. You might take a picture. You will not know why it feels important yet.

Then a message arrives, and there it is. Another orange shovel, in another town, at almost the same hour. DES. The universe has a sense of humour, and today it is wearing hi-vis. Spend the evening wondering what the shovels want. The answer is probably nothing, which is the funniest answer of all.
nancy.mission: Ask someone today what the most suspicious object in their neighbourhood is, and listen to the whole story.
nancy.omen: Something orange in the snow. It means a happy coincidence is circling and about to land.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's stone, ready for matching shovels

together.text: Two orange shovels, two towns, one afternoon. ΔΕΣ, obviously. Agree on what the shovels are trying to tell you and write it down as an official prophecy. Then check back in a month and see whether the shovels were right.

title: The Tiger and the Rat Throw a Party
skyStory: Lunar New Year arrives under a perfectly dark new moon in Aquarius, zero percent light, which means every lantern on Earth gets to be the moon tonight. The Goat steps up to take its year. The Fire Tiger and the Wood Rat watch from the cabin porch, waving at the new arrival, offering it a cup of something warm and a seat by the fire.

reading: The zodiac animals are changing shifts, and the Tiger gets a little nostalgic watching the old year pack up. That is allowed. Raise an imaginary cup to everything you built last year, even the half-finished pieces leaning in the corner.

Then welcome the new year the way you welcome friends: loudly, warmly, with too much enthusiasm. Hang something red in a window. A ribbon, a scarf, a paper lantern you folded badly. [[The Sun]] would like you to let a celebration happen without organizing every second of it. Let someone else light the candles.
joel.mission: Hang something red in a window for the new year and leave it there for at least three days.
joel.omen: A red light glowing in a neighbour's window. It means good fortune has found your street.
joel.stoneWhy: red for the new year

reading: Of all the animals, the Rat was the cleverest in the great race, and everyone knows it. Today the Wood Rat stands a little taller. You see three moves ahead, and the new year knows it is lucky to have you on its side.

Give yourself a small new year ritual. Sweep one doorway, out toward the door, to clear the old year away. Then open a window for exactly ten seconds and let the cold February air rush in like a guest who brought gossip. Close it. Smile. The year has officially begun.
nancy.mission: Sweep one doorway outward to clear the old year, then open a window for ten seconds to let the new one in.
nancy.omen: A goat on a sign, a sweater or a cheese label. It means the new year likes you already.
nancy.elementWhy: fresh air for a fresh year

together.text: Each of you picks one wish for the other for the Year of the Goat. Make it specific: more lazy Sundays, one perfect beach day, a story that makes a whole room laugh. Send it with a red heart. The Tiger and the Rat throw excellent parties.

title: The Great Sock Amnesty
skyStory: One percent of a moon peeks out of Aquarius, the thinnest eyelash of light, and declares a cosmic amnesty. All lost things may return without punishment. Socks, pens, the remote, a forgotten idea from July. Saturn grumbles about precedent. Mars says let them come home. The moon sides with Mars for once, and the universe sighs happily.

reading: A lazy Sunday has been declared, and the cabin approves. Sleep in if you can. Wear the softest thing you own. If anyone asks what you are doing today, the official answer is recharging, and it is said with total confidence.

Somewhere in your laundry pile lives a sock that lost its partner in October. Today it reunites. Hold the pair up to the light like a trophy. The [[Six of Pentacles]] notes that you are capable of receiving small mercies, even from a dryer. Practice on the sock. Work up to people.
joel.mission: Find one lost thing today, celebrate its return with a small speech, and put it somewhere it will never vanish again.
joel.omen: Two mismatched socks side by side. It means a friendly reunion is coming your way this week.
joel.stoneWhy: comfort on the receiving wrist
joel.elementWhy: a soft day for soft things

reading: Rest is not a reward you have to earn, says the moon, very seriously, from behind a cloud. You know this. You tell other people this. Today you get to practice what you preach, preferably under a blanket with a story you have been meaning to finish.

The shore is quiet and wintry. Somewhere, ice is creaking politely along the edge of the water. Let the day be shapeless. If a small chore appears, give it a polite nod and walk past it like a cat ignoring a call. The [[Nine of Cups]] wants to see you satisfied without anything to prove.
nancy.mission: Spend thirty minutes doing something purely for fun, and refuse to explain it to anyone.
nancy.omen: Ice crystals on a window shaped like ferns. It means rest today grows something lovely tomorrow.
nancy.stoneWhy: soft shimmer for a soft day

together.text: Declare a joint lazy Sunday. Text each other only once, at exactly 3 pm, with a single word describing your current level of cosiness. Bonus points for inventing a new word. The universe is officially closed for maintenance until Monday.

title: The Day the Kettle Dreamed
skyStory: The moon swims into Pisces, still mostly hidden at four percent, and the whole sky goes a little dreamy and wet around the edges. Pisces is the sign of fish, fog and daydreams, and tonight it whispers soft nonsense to every kettle in Atlantic Canada. The kettles whistle back in harmony. Saturn pretends it cannot hear. It is humming along.

reading: Monday arrives in slippers. Your brain will feel like a snow globe someone just shook, all sparkle and no direction. Give it until 10 am to settle. Meanwhile, do the easiest task on your list and call it momentum.

In the afternoon, you will have a strange little daydream, something about a boat, or a bridge, or a cabin with a second chimney. Do not dismiss it. Pisces sends ideas in disguise. Sketch it on the back of an envelope. The [[Page of Cups]] is peeking around the corner, holding a fish, delighted that you noticed.
joel.mission: Doodle the strangest daydream you have today, however badly, and keep the drawing until the end of the week.
joel.omen: A kettle that whistles a moment early. It means an idea is ready before you think it is.
joel.stoneWhy: Pisces loves anything from the sea

reading: Fog rolls in off the shore of your imagination today. Things look softer. People seem kinder. Even the slush on the sidewalk has a certain poetic quality, if you squint and are wearing very good boots.

Someone will tell you a story that does not quite make sense, and the Wood Rat in you will spot the missing piece in about four seconds. Hand it back to them gently, like returning a dropped mitten. Your intuition is a lighthouse today. The Life Path 11 beam is on full, sweeping across the water.
nancy.mission: Notice the first piece of fog, steam or mist you see today and make a wish on it.
nancy.omen: A fish shape somewhere unexpected, on a sign or a mug. It means trust your gut on a decision this week.
nancy.stoneWhy: a lighthouse needs a clear lens

together.text: Describe your perfect foggy morning to each other in three sentences. Where are you, what are you holding, what can you hear. Pisces will collect both answers and blend them into one shared dream, delivered sometime this week while you sleep.

title: The Message in the Foggy Window
skyStory: A sliver of waxing crescent returns at eight percent, still splashing around in Pisces like a kid who refuses to leave the pool. The moon is growing again, which means everything you planted on the new moon is quietly sprouting underground. Mars peers down, impatient. Saturn hands it a book called Waiting Well. Mars uses it as a coaster.

reading: The bathroom mirror will steam up this morning and practically beg you to write in it. So write in it. Something encouraging, something ridiculous, something for future-you to discover the next time the shower runs hot.

At work or wherever you are, a teammate will be struggling with a problem you solved once before. You will want to swoop in and fix it entirely. Instead, ask one good question and let them find the answer. Teaching is your Life Path 3 superpower, and watching someone else light up is a better reward than being the hero.
joel.mission: Write a short secret message in a steamy mirror or a frosted window for someone to discover later.
joel.omen: Fingerprints on glass in a heart or star shape. It means someone has been thinking warmly about you.
joel.stoneWhy: layered wisdom for teaching moments

reading: The moon is growing, and so is something in you. You might not feel it yet. It is the quiet kind of growth, the kind that happens underground in February while the snow sits on top looking unimpressed.

Around 2:20 pm you will notice that a skill you have been practising is suddenly easier. Do not brush past it. Stop. Point at it like a birdwatcher spotting something rare. The [[Six of Swords]] is moving steadily across the water. Each little improvement is another oar stroke, and you are much further from the shore you left than you realise.
nancy.mission: Name out loud one thing you can do now that you could not do a year ago.
nancy.omen: A tiny green sprout or a houseplant with a new leaf. It means your effort is about to show.

together.text: Trade one small progress report each, something you are better at than last month. Then each pay the other one sincere, slightly over-the-top compliment about it. Saturn will roll its eyes. The moon will glow approximately one percent brighter.

title: The Moon Moves Into the Cabin
skyStory: At fifteen percent, the crescent bounds into Aries, Joel's own sign, and kicks the cabin door open like it owns the place. It tosses its coat on a chair and asks what is for dinner. Mars, ruler of Aries, is thrilled to have company. The two of them start planning a project before the woodstove has even caught. The cabin chimney puffs happily.

reading: The moon has come to visit your sign, and you will feel it the moment you wake up. Energy. Ideas. An urge to rearrange the furniture before breakfast. The Tiger is up and pacing, tail flicking. Point it at something useful.

The [[Knight of Wands]] rides alongside today, but it carries a single torch, not a bundle. Pick the one project that makes you grin and give it two good hours. Two. Then stop while it is still exciting. The trick to starting fires is knowing when to let them burn on their own.
joel.mission: Give one project two focused hours, then walk away while you still want more.
joel.omen: A red car, a red hat, or a red mailbox catching sunlight. It means Mars is cheering you on.
joel.stoneWhy: an anchor for a racing Tiger

reading: With the moon in Joel's sign, you might catch a little of his spark today. You will want to start something. You might even start it. Your steady Capricorn hands paired with borrowed Aries fire are a dangerous combination, in the best possible way.

Around 11 am, an idea arrives that seems too bold for a Wednesday in February. It is not. Write it down. Saturn and Mars are clinking mugs somewhere up there, impressed with themselves for once. Mountain meets fire. Let the spark catch on something you care about.
nancy.mission: Say yes to one small adventure today that you would usually save for later.
nancy.omen: A flame flickering in a window or on a candle. It means Joel is sending a spark your way.

together.text: Joel, switch the onyx to your right wrist for one hour today and send a spark down the line. Nancy, tap the ruby twice when you feel it. Neither of you will be able to prove it worked. Both of you will know.

title: The Day of the Matching Typo
skyStory: Twenty-three percent of the moon blazes in Aries, and Mars has had three coffees. Every message sent today travels slightly faster than it should, and some arrive with spelling mistakes that nobody can explain. The moon thinks this is hilarious. Somewhere in the universe, a cosmic spell checker has taken a personal day and left a note saying good luck.

reading: You will type the word winter as wintre today. Not once. Twice. Your fingers seem to have decided that February is spelled differently in the cabin. Fix it the first time. The second time, leave it. Let it be charming.

That evening, Nancy will send you a message with the exact same typo. Same word, same swapped letters, same hour. DES. Neither of you will be able to explain it. The Aries moon simply sent one gremlin to two keyboards and called it a job well done. Screenshot both and keep them forever.
joel.mission: Send someone a message today with one deliberate silly typo and see if they notice.
joel.omen: A misspelled sign on a shop window or a menu board. It means a funny coincidence is incoming.
joel.stoneWhy: sharp eyes to spot the gremlin

reading: Your words are quick today, a bit faster than usual, and occasionally they trip over each other. That is fine. The story still lands. Your hands fill in the gaps, as always, and everyone leans in a little closer.

Around 7 pm your keyboard betrays you with a strange typo, and you will catch it just after hitting send. Do not apologise. Then Joel replies with the very same mistake, and the room goes quiet for a second. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] spins once with a little click. Don't even scream. Just frame it.
nancy.mission: Tell one story today entirely with your hands for the first ten seconds before saying a word.
nancy.omen: Two kids in the same dinosaur toque waiting at the same crosswalk. A matching moment is already on its way.

together.text: The typo twins have struck. ΔΕΣ, absolutely. Decide what your shared misspelling secretly means and use it as a code word for the rest of the month. Whenever one of you sends it, the other has to reply with a terrible pun.

title: The Day of the Very Slow Bull
skyStory: The moon reaches its first quarter in Taurus, a third lit and in no hurry whatsoever. Taurus is a bull that lies in a sunny field and refuses to move until the grass gets interesting. Mars tries to herd it. The bull yawns. Saturn sits down beside the bull and says, honestly, this is nice. They watch the clouds together until dusk.

reading: After two days of Aries fire, the moon slows down to a stroll, and it would like you to slow down too. Not stop. Stroll. Walk instead of rush. Read the whole message before replying. Taste your coffee before the mug is empty.

There will be a moment around 3:30 pm when something takes longer than it should, and you will feel the familiar tug of impatience. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] is the slowest knight in the deck, and he gets there anyway. Every time. Breathe. Count the snowflakes on the window if you have to.
joel.mission: Do one ordinary task today at half your normal speed, like a nature documentary about yourself.
joel.omen: A slow-moving truck in front of you, or a long line. It means patience is paying off somewhere else.
joel.stoneWhy: smooth and calm, like slow water

reading: Taurus and Capricorn get along beautifully. Both are earth signs, both stubborn in the most loyal way. Today the universe moves at your speed for once, and you will feel almost smug about it. Go ahead. Be a little smug.

You will finish something that has been dragging on for weeks, quietly, without fanfare. No one will notice at first. Then someone will, probably on Monday, and they will be impressed. The Wood Rat knows the best victories are the ones nobody saw coming, built one patient step at a time.
nancy.mission: Finish one lingering task today and celebrate it privately with your favourite mug.
nancy.omen: A cow, a bull, or a field of snow with a single set of footprints. It means steady wins the day.
nancy.stoneWhy: small steps, stacked into something sparkly
nancy.elementWhy: both of you love solid ground

together.text: Have the slowest conversation of the year. One message every hour, each building on the last, like passing notes in class. By bedtime you will have one ridiculous little story written together, and the bull will finally be impressed.

title: The Day of the Good Blanket
skyStory: Forty-three percent of the moon lounges in Taurus, still comfortable, still unbothered. Taurus has found the good blanket, the heavy one, and it is not sharing. Saturn tries to borrow a corner. Mars brings snacks as a bribe. The moon finally relents and spreads the blanket over the whole sky. Even the snowbanks below look cosier tonight.

reading: Saturday rolls in heavy and warm, like a cat settling onto your lap. The Tiger wants to do something. The Taurus moon wants to do nothing. Negotiate. Maybe one small adventure in the morning, then the blanket by noon.

This afternoon, someone will offer you something nice, a cup of tea or a compliment or the good chair. Your instinct will be to refuse, politely, and offer it back. The [[Six of Pentacles]] is waving its arms. Accept it. Receive it. Sit in the good chair like it was built for you. It was.
joel.mission: Accept every small kindness offered to you today with a plain thank you and zero protest.
joel.omen: A blanket hung over a balcony railing or a clothesline. It means comfort is coming your way.
joel.stoneWhy: warm red for a cosy day

reading: There is a particular kind of February Saturday that smells like woodsmoke and bread, and today is it. Even if nobody is baking. Even if the stove is electric. The air simply decides to smell that way, and you get to enjoy it.

Find the best blanket in the house and claim it. If anyone asks, you are conducting important Saturn research on comfort. By late afternoon, an old friend or an old memory will drift in, warm and unexpected. Let it stay for a while. The [[Four of Cups]] is offering something good. Take it.
nancy.mission: Claim the coziest seat in your home for at least an hour and defend it with a dignified look.
nancy.omen: Steam rising from a mug in a sunbeam. It means a happy memory is on its way to visit.
nancy.stoneWhy: soft glow for a soft day

together.text: Send each other a photo of your blanket situation at exactly 4 pm. Rate each other's on a scale of one to ten mountains. Tomorrow is a day for friends, so rest up, because the Gemini moon has big plans for both of you.

title: Valentine's Day for the Best of Pals
skyStory: The moon is half lit and dancing into Gemini, the sign of the twins, which makes it the perfect patron for a day about friends. Gemini loves a good chat, a shared joke, two voices finishing each other's sentences. Mars and Saturn, usually clashing like thunder, exchange handmade cards. Saturn's is very neat. Mars's has glitter everywhere. Both are perfect.

reading: Today is for every friend who ever shovelled your driveway, laughed at your worst joke, or sat with you in a quiet room. Valentine's Day was secretly invented for friendship, and the Gemini moon will not hear otherwise.

Write three short notes to three friends. Say exactly what they mean to you, no hedging. The [[Three of Cups]] is raising a glass in your direction. And when Nancy sends you something today, receive it fully. You give so much. Let the Tiger be the one who gets the card for once.
joel.mission: Write three short notes to three friends saying one specific thing you love about each of them.
joel.omen: A paper heart taped to a window or a door. It means someone is grateful you exist.
joel.stoneWhy: Nancy's stone, worn with gratitude

reading: Your friends are your mountain range. You are one peak, but you were never meant to stand alone, and today the Gemini moon reminds you of every voice that ever cheered you on from the next summit over.

Tell a friend a story today about the moment you knew they were your people. Use your hands. Use the dramatic pause. The ruby on your pinky will catch the light just as you get to the good part. That is Joel, cheering from the cabin. Friendship like this is its own kind of fire.
nancy.mission: Tell a friend the story of how you first knew they were one of your people.
nancy.omen: Two birds sitting side by side on a wire. It means your friendships are stronger than any February.

together.text: Swap stones in spirit today. Joel touches the onyx, Nancy touches the ruby, both at noon, both thinking of the other. Then send one sentence each: a thank you for something the other never knew helped. Friendship is the best Valentine there is.

title: The Day of Two Loud Opinions
skyStory: The Gemini moon swells to sixty-five percent and splits into two voices, each convinced it is right. One says the snow is pretty. The other says the snow is in the way. They argue all afternoon over the long weekend Monday, and the sky is far too entertained to break it up. Saturn takes notes for a debate club.

reading: A holiday Monday in the middle of February is a small gift from the calendar, and the Tiger plans to unwrap it slowly. Two voices in your head will argue about how to spend it. One wants a project. One wants pancakes and a nap.

Let them both win. Morning for the project, afternoon for the nap. Around 2 pm you will get into a cheerful debate with someone about something unimportant, like the correct way to stack a woodpile. Argue passionately. Lose gracefully. The [[Two of Swords]] says some arguments exist purely for sport, and this is one.
joel.mission: Start a friendly, totally pointless debate today and make your case like it is a courtroom drama.
joel.omen: Two people pointing in opposite directions. It means both paths are good, so pick the funnier one.
joel.stoneWhy: many facets for many opinions
joel.elementWhy: Gemini talks a mile a minute

reading: The Wood Rat enjoys a long weekend the way a cat enjoys a sunbeam: fully, with no apology. Today you will hear two sides of a small story from two different people, and you will be the only one who sees the whole picture.

Do not referee. Just smile and say, interesting. The Gemini moon loves a puzzle, and you are the one who can solve it without saying a word. Later, tell your own version of the story to someone who will appreciate it, with hand gestures for both sides. It will be a hit.
nancy.mission: Tell one story today doing two different voices for two different characters.
nancy.omen: A mirror or a window reflecting two of something. It means you can see both sides clearly today.
nancy.elementWhy: the calm centre of the chatter

together.text: Pick a silly question, like whether snowmen should wear hats or scarves, and take opposite sides. Argue by message all day with escalating seriousness. At sundown, swap sides and argue the other way. Gemini will award the trophy.

title: The Day of Forty Open Tabs
skyStory: The moon is a waxing gibbous now, seventy-six percent bright and still lingering in Gemini, curious about absolutely everything. It has opened forty tabs on the cosmic browser. Comets, recipes, the history of mittens. Mars says, close some. The moon says, but they are all interesting. Saturn quietly bookmarks the important ones for later and closes the rest.

reading: Your curiosity is at full power, and that is both your gift and your trap today. You will start reading about one thing and end up, two hours later, knowing far too much about the migratory habits of eider ducks.

That is fine, in moderation. But the [[Knight of Wands]] is clearing his throat. Choose one rabbit hole for the day and explore it properly. Then teach someone what you learned at dinner, in your best storytelling voice. A Life Path 3 should never waste a good fact. Bonus points if the fact involves ducks.
joel.mission: Learn one weird fact today and teach it to someone before bedtime with full enthusiasm.
joel.omen: A duck, real or on a sign. It means your curiosity is about to lead somewhere useful.
joel.stoneWhy: calm water for a busy brain

reading: Your mind is a lighthouse sweeping across a wide grey sea today, catching glimpses of a dozen interesting ships. Do not chase them all. Pick one, the most curious looking one, and follow it to harbour.

Around 4:15 pm someone will mention a book, a show or an idea in passing. Write it down. The Wood Rat knows that the best treasures arrive disguised as small talk. This one is going to matter later, maybe in April. Your Life Path 11 is already humming about it, quietly, like a kettle just before it sings.
nancy.mission: Write down one thing someone mentions in passing today and look into it before the week is out.
nancy.omen: A boat or a ship in a picture or on a mug. It means a good idea is sailing toward you.
nancy.stoneWhy: a clear beam for the lighthouse
nancy.elementWhy: ideas carried in on sea breezes

together.text: Send each other the single strangest fact you learned this week. No explanation, no context, just the fact. The other has to reply with a question. Gemini loves a curious pair, and the universe is a library that never closes.

title: The Shell on the Windowsill
skyStory: Eighty-five percent of the moon settles into Cancer, the crab, which carries its home on its back and never feels lost. Cancer is the moon's own favourite sign, and tonight it glows like a porch light left on for someone coming home late. Saturn admits, grudgingly, that it likes a cosy house. Mars brings a housewarming plant.

reading: The cabin feels extra warm today, even if the windows rattle. You will notice small things you love about your home: the way the light hits the counter at 3 pm, the creak in one particular floorboard, the mug that fits your hand exactly.

Make one small improvement to your space. Move a lamp. Hang a picture that has been leaning against the wall since autumn. The [[Ten of Cups]] is smiling over your shoulder. Home is not a place you have to earn. It is a place you get to enjoy.
joel.mission: Hang, move or fix one small thing in your home that you have been ignoring for weeks.
joel.omen: A porch light glowing in daylight. It means someone is thinking of you as home.
joel.stoneWhy: home is where Nancy's stone sits

reading: There is a seashell somewhere in your home, maybe on a windowsill, maybe in a drawer, picked up on a summer day years ago. Today it hums. Hold it up to your ear and you will hear the shore, waiting for you, patient as you are.

The Cancer moon makes everything feel tender. A text from an old friend, a song on the radio, a smell of woodsmoke on the walk home. Let yourself feel all of it. You are the mountain, steady and strong, but even mountains have warm valleys tucked away.
nancy.mission: Find a keepsake from a beach day, hold it for a minute, and remember exactly where you found it.
nancy.omen: A shell, a pebble, or a piece of sea glass in an unexpected place. It means summer is closer than it looks.
nancy.elementWhy: the crab's home is the tide

together.text: Describe your favourite corner of your home to each other, in exact detail: what you can see, what you can hear, what is within arm's reach. Then plan an imaginary visit, cabin to shore and back again. The moon is leaving the porch light on.

title: The Blue Jay Who Visited Twice
skyStory: The waxing gibbous moon swells to ninety-two percent in Cancer, and its silver light reaches into every bird feeder in the province. Cancer is sentimental and slightly psychic, and tonight it has hatched a plan involving one bossy blue jay and two separate windows. The moon refuses to say more. It just hums and polishes itself for the full moon.

reading: At around 10:12 am a blue jay will land somewhere near you, scream once with incredible confidence, and leave. You will laugh. It will feel like a message, though you cannot tell what it says. Note the time.

Later Nancy will tell you a blue jay screamed at her too, at 10:12 am, in her own yard, miles away. DES. [[The Star]] is twinkling with satisfaction. Somewhere, a single very busy bird is delivering the same memo across the whole region. Your only job is to receive it with appropriate astonishment.
joel.mission: Write down the exact time of the first bird you hear today, then compare notes with Nancy.
joel.omen: A single sunflower husk on your doorstep. Someone far away is noticing the same small wonder at the same moment.
joel.stoneWhy: clear sight for bird messages

reading: The Wood Rat hears the blue jay before anyone else does: a single, outrageous shriek outside the window at 10:12 am. You will look up, startled, then grin. Birds do not usually scream that confidently unless they know something.

When Joel sends his message, you will check the time and go very quiet. Same bird, same scream, same minute. Don't even scream, the jay did it for you. The Cancer moon loves a cosmic connection, and today it has tied a blue ribbon between two windows. Keep the ribbon. Tie it somewhere you will see it all week.
nancy.mission: Leave a small treat out for the birds today and name the first visitor something grand.
nancy.omen: A flash of blue at the edge of your vision. It means a matching moment has already happened.

together.text: ΔΕΣ for the blue jay. Give that bird an official title, something like Sir Screams-a-Lot, Royal Messenger of the Cabin and the Shore. Then each leave out a small treat for the birds as payment for services rendered.

title: The Lion Warms Up the Stage
skyStory: The full moon roars into Leo at ninety-eight percent, golden and theatrical, sweeping its silver cape across a sky full of snow clouds. Leo loves an audience and a spotlight, and tonight the moon is both. It practices its bows. Mars applauds from the front row. Saturn, in the back, clapping politely, is secretly moved. Tomorrow is the big show.

reading: Fire signs love a Leo moon, and you will feel it in your chest like a drumroll. Today you get the spotlight, maybe in a meeting, maybe at dinner, maybe just in your own kitchen. Take it. Speak up. Tell the story fully.

But [[The Sun]] is reversed for you two, a gentle reminder that joy should be allowed, not earned. So when the applause comes, do not deflect it with a joke. Take the bow. The Tiger and the Lion are cousins, and cousins know how to soak up a little glory.
joel.mission: When someone praises your work today, take a real bow, literally, from the waist.
joel.omen: A golden light in a window at dusk. It means the spotlight is yours tonight.
joel.stoneWhy: red-gold for a Leo moon
joel.elementWhy: the Lion and the Tiger roar

reading: Leo moons make storytellers glow, and you are a storyteller to the bone. Tonight someone will ask you to tell a story you have told before. Tell it bigger. Add a dramatic pause. Let your hands do a full performance.

The audience will be small, maybe one person, maybe the cat, but it will be the best version of that story ever told. Saturn, your ruler, quietly approves of a well-rehearsed classic. Then, tomorrow night, get ready for something special. The full moon is setting the stage just for you two.
nancy.mission: Retell your favourite story tonight with at least one dramatic pause and one big hand flourish.
nancy.omen: A lion on a sign, a flag or a statue. It means your voice carries further than you think.

together.text: Tomorrow is the Full Moon Recharge. Tonight, find a spot near a window where the moonlight will fall, and clear it like a stage. Tell each other where your spot is. The ruby and the onyx have a date with the sky.

title: The Great February Recharge
skyStory: The moon reaches one hundred percent, perfectly full in Leo, and the snowbanks shine like a stage lit for a finale. This is the Full Moon Recharge. Every stone on Earth turns toward the light, but two in particular, a ruby and an onyx, hum with special attention. Mars and Saturn stand side by side, for once agreeing completely. Tonight belongs to them.

reading: Tonight, take off the onyx bracelet and set it on a windowsill where the full moon will find it. Next to it, if you can, place something red, to stand in for Nancy's ruby. The two stones will soak up the moonlight together, recharging from across the miles.

While they charge, think about everything you have given this month: your time, your ideas, your fire. Then think about what you have received. The [[Six of Pentacles]] wants the second list to be as long as the first. It will not be yet. But it is getting longer.
joel.mission: Set the onyx on a windowsill under tonight's full moon and leave it there until morning.
joel.omen: Moonlight falling across the floor in a long silver stripe. It means the recharge has begun.
joel.stoneWhy: the Full Moon Recharge needs onyx

reading: Slide the ruby off your right pinky tonight and set it in the moonlight, on a windowsill or a table. Beside it, if you have one nearby, place the onyx bracelet from your left wrist. Fire and earth, side by side, catching the same light.

The full moon in Leo is generous, and it will fill both stones right up. As they charge, let yourself feel the [[Six of Swords]] gliding forward. The crossing is still happening, but tonight the water is calm and silver. Joel is rowing too. You can feel the oars moving in rhythm.
nancy.mission: Set the ruby and onyx side by side under the full moon tonight and make one wish over them.
nancy.omen: A clear patch of sky right where the moon is. It means the universe made room for the recharge.
nancy.elementWhy: the ruby is the fire stone

together.text: At 9 pm, both stones go into the moonlight. Send each other a photo of your windowsill setup, then stay quiet for one minute while the stones charge. Fire Tiger and Wood Rat, cabin and shore, all under one very bright moon.

title: The Day of the Tidy Afterglow
skyStory: The full moon slides into Virgo, still ninety-nine percent bright, and immediately starts tidying up after last night's party. It sweeps up the stardust, folds the clouds, and puts the stones back on their wearers with tiny notes attached. Virgo is the sign of order and detail. Saturn nods in deep approval. Mars is still asleep on the couch.

reading: The onyx goes back on your left wrist this morning, freshly charged, and you will feel it hum slightly for an hour or so. The world looks sharper today. Details jump out at you: a typo in a sign, a crooked frame, a bird you have never noticed before.

Virgo energy wants you to fix little things, but gently. Pick three small details to set right, then let the rest be imperfect. The [[Eight of Swords]] reminds you that perfection is a cage made of thoughts. Step out of it. The afterglow is better when you are not straightening it.
joel.mission: Fix exactly three small imperfections today and deliberately leave a fourth one alone.
joel.omen: A crooked picture frame. Straighten it, and a small worry will straighten itself by evening.
joel.stoneWhy: smooth, calm, freshly charged

reading: The ruby returns to your pinky, still glowing from last night, and the purplish-pink stone seems brighter in the morning light. The Wood Rat feels sharp and capable today, full of plans that actually have steps.

Virgo and Capricorn are both earth signs, and they get along like two librarians who love the same shelving system. Use this energy to organise one small corner of your life. Then stop and admire it. You do not have to tidy everything. One corner is a whole victory, and Saturn will absolutely write it in the logbook.
nancy.mission: Organise one drawer, shelf or folder today, then show it to someone like a museum curator.
nancy.omen: A neatly folded blanket or a stack of books. It means your plans are falling into place.

together.text: Each of you lets go of one small thing that has been bothering you, a minor annoyance or a messy corner. Name it, release it, and send the other a single word: done. The full moon is packing up, and it is taking the clutter with it.

title: The Case of the Missing Lid
skyStory: The moon begins to wane, ninety-six percent and still in fussy Virgo, counting every container in the cosmic cupboard. There are forty-one containers. There are thirty-eight lids. Virgo is beside itself. Saturn launches a formal inquiry. Mars suggests just using a plate on top, and the whole sky gasps in horror. The inquiry runs well past midnight.

reading: A small mystery will consume a ridiculous amount of your attention today. A lid, a key, a charging cable that was right here five minutes ago. You will search with the intensity of a detective in a rainstorm, muttering theories under your breath.

Here is the secret: it is under something blue. The Virgo moon will not tell you more than that. While you search, notice how much energy you give to small problems, and how good it feels when you finally solve one. The [[Page of Pentacles]] is cheering. Victory is victory, however tiny the lid.
joel.mission: When you find something you lost today, announce the discovery like a news anchor breaking a story.
joel.omen: Something blue sitting on top of something else. Look under it, because a small mystery is about to end.
joel.stoneWhy: sharp eyes for the great search
joel.elementWhy: clear the cobwebs, find the lid

reading: The Wood Rat finds things. That is simply a fact. Today someone near you will lose something, and you will spot it within a minute, sitting in plain sight, being smug about it. They will call you a genius. Accept the title.

Later, you will notice a mismatch somewhere: a calendar that says the wrong day, a sock that is not quite the same shade as its partner. Leave one mismatch alone, on purpose. Virgo will twitch. Saturn will understand. Some things are more charming slightly wrong, and you know exactly which ones.
nancy.mission: Help someone find a lost thing today, then refuse to explain how you knew where it was.
nancy.omen: A lid that does not fit its container. It means a small rule can be broken without consequence.
nancy.elementWhy: go with the flow of mysteries

together.text: Each of you hides one small object somewhere in your home in plain sight, then describes the hiding spot to the other in a riddle. The other gets three guesses. Whoever stumps the other wins the title of Supreme Finder for the week.

title: The Day of the Balanced Spoon
skyStory: Ninety percent of the moon tips into Libra, the sign of scales and balance, and immediately tries to balance a spoon on its nose. It almost works. Libra is all about fairness and harmony, and tonight it wants everything level: the pictures on the wall, the snow on both sides of the driveway, the conversation between Mars and Saturn.

reading: Libra is weighing your week today, and it has noticed something: you have given a great deal and received very little. The scales are tipping. Libra wants them level, and it is going to arrange some help for you whether you like it or not.

Around 1 pm someone will offer to take something off your plate. A task, a chore, a worry. The [[Six of Pentacles]] is standing right behind them, nodding vigorously. Say yes. Let the scale tip back. The Tiger can carry the world, but today the Tiger is allowed to put it down for a bit.
joel.mission: Let someone help you with one task today, without offering to help them back right away.
joel.omen: A spoon, fork or pen balanced on the edge of something. It means harmony is restoring itself.
joel.stoneWhy: soft balance for a heavy week

reading: Your sense of fairness is extra sharp under a Libra moon. You will notice who has been talking too much in a meeting and who has not been heard at all. Gently, without fuss, you will turn toward the quiet one and ask what they think.

That one question will change the whole conversation. People will remember it later, though they will not know exactly why. That is the magic of a Life Path 11: you level up the room without anyone noticing you did it. Saturn, watching from above, is very proud of you.
nancy.mission: Ask the quietest person you talk to today what they think, and really listen to the answer.
nancy.omen: A set of scales on a sign or a picture. It means your sense of fairness is about to help someone.

together.text: Each of you lists three things you gave this week and three things you received. Compare the lists. Whoever has the shorter received column has to accept one compliment from the other, with no deflection, no joke, just a thank you. Libra is watching closely.

title: The Day of the Even Trade
skyStory: The waning gibbous moon shrinks to eighty-three percent, still in Libra, and opens a little cosmic swap shop. Trade a worry for a laugh. Trade a grey morning for a bright afternoon. Saturn trades a stern look for a reluctant smile. Mars trades five half-finished ideas for one good one, and the moon declares it the bargain of the century.

reading: Your brain is holding five half-finished projects, and every one of them is waving at you from the corner of your mind like an excited puppy. The [[Knight of Wands]] has seen enough. Today, trade four of them for one.

Not forever. Just for this week. Write the other four on a list and put them in a drawer. Then aim the full fire of the Tiger at the one that remains. By Friday you will have something finished, and the drawer will still be there, waiting patiently with its puppies.
joel.mission: Write your four least urgent projects on a list, put it in a drawer, and focus on one.
joel.omen: Two people swapping something, a glove or a book or a seat. It means a good exchange is coming your way.
joel.stoneWhy: steady focus for one project
joel.elementWhy: aim the fire at one thing

reading: Someone will offer you a trade today, and it will be a good one. Maybe a task swapped for a favour, maybe a seat by the window swapped for one by the door. The Wood Rat weighs it in two seconds flat and knows instantly.

Take the trade. Then make one of your own: swap a familiar habit for something new, even just for the day. A different mug. A different walk. A different first sentence when you answer the phone. Libra loves a little exchange, and so do you, secretly.
nancy.mission: Swap one small habit for something new today and notice what changes, even slightly.
nancy.omen: A coin or a button on the ground. It means a fair trade is about to land in your lap.
nancy.elementWhy: steady footing in the swap shop

together.text: Trade one task with each other, just for fun. Nancy picks something for Joel to do today, Joel picks something for Nancy. Keep them small and silly: hum a tune at lunch, wear a hat indoors for an hour. The swap shop closes at midnight.

title: The Twin Snowmen of Late February
skyStory: The moon slips into Scorpio, seventy-five percent lit and mysterious, wearing a dark cloak and an expression that says it knows something you do not. Scorpio loves secrets and strange connections. Tonight it has quietly arranged for two snowmen, built by two different strangers in two different towns, to wear exactly the same unusual hat. The moon winks once.

reading: On your way somewhere today you will pass a snowman wearing a striped toque, one pinecone eye and one bottle-cap eye, holding a wooden spoon up to its face like a microphone. You will laugh out loud. You will take a photo because it is too good not to.

That evening, Nancy will send you a photo of a snowman in her town: striped toque, pinecone eye, bottle-cap eye, wooden spoon microphone. DES. Two snowmen, built by two strangers, miles apart. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] is clearly in a playful mood. Accept that the universe has a sense of humour.
joel.mission: Photograph a snowman, a frost pattern, or an icicle that looks like it has a personality.
joel.omen: A snowman with mismatched eyes. Somewhere, a second snowman is wearing the exact same grin.
joel.stoneWhy: the stone Nancy wears, for matching snowmen

reading: Scorpio moons sharpen your intuition to a point, and today you will feel a strange little pull to take the long way home. Follow it. Halfway along you will meet a snowman in a striped toque with mismatched eyes and a wooden spoon raised mid-song, looking at you like an old friend.

Then your phone buzzes, and there is the same snowman in Joel's photo, miles away. Same toque, same eyes, same spoon held up for the big finale. Don't even scream. The Wood Rat knew something was coming. Your Life Path 11 has been humming all week, and now you know why.
nancy.mission: Take a slightly different route somewhere today and look closely at everything you pass.
nancy.omen: A wooden spoon somewhere it does not belong, like a windowsill or a mailbox. A coincidence is about to come and find you.
nancy.stoneWhy: the stone Joel wears, for matching snowmen

together.text: The twin snowmen have spoken. ΔΕΣ, without question. Give them names together, matching ones, and decide what they would say to each other if they ever met. Write their imaginary conversation in exactly six lines, three each, by bedtime.

title: The Day of the Secret Drawer
skyStory: The last quarter moon settles in Scorpio, sixty-five percent lit and halfway through its exhale. Scorpio is the sign of hidden things, and tonight it gently opens a secret drawer in the sky. Inside: old worries, folded neatly, waiting to be let go. The moon picks them up one at a time and releases them into the dark like moths.

reading: There is a drawer in your home, or maybe in your mind, where you keep things you have not dealt with. An old note. A to-do list from last spring. An idea you never quite started. Today the waning moon wants you to open it.

Take out one item and decide its fate. Keep it, finish it, or let it go. The [[Death]] card is just about endings that make room, nothing scarier. Releasing one small thing will feel like opening a window in a stuffy room. The cabin breathes easier, and so do you.
joel.mission: Open a forgotten drawer today and let go of one thing inside it, with a short farewell speech.
joel.omen: An old receipt or note found in a coat pocket. It means a forgotten chapter is ready to close.
joel.stoneWhy: layers ready to be sorted

reading: Scorpio is digging around in the corners of your thoughts today, and it will find one small worry you have been carrying around for weeks without noticing. It is lighter than you thought. It might even be out of date.

The [[Eight of Swords]] is reminding you that some cages are made entirely of thoughts, and the door has been unlocked the whole time. Name the worry out loud. Then let it go, like a leaf dropped into a stream. Watch it float away. The mountain stands a little taller without it.
nancy.mission: Write one old worry on a scrap of paper, then tear it into tiny pieces and toss it away.
nancy.omen: A moth or a leaf drifting past a window. It means something heavy is lifting from your shoulders.
nancy.stoneWhy: a gentle release, like the tide

together.text: Each of you releases one small thing today: an old worry, an outdated plan, a grudge against a stubborn jar lid. Tell each other what it was, in one sentence, then never mention it again. The waning moon will carry both away tonight.

title: The Arrow Pointing Toward March
skyStory: The moon gallops into Sagittarius at fifty-six percent, the archer drawing its bow and aiming straight at March. Sagittarius is optimistic, adventurous and slightly reckless, and it has heard rumours of an equinox birthday coming up. The arrow flies across the sky and lands somewhere near the cabin. Mars cheers. Saturn checks the date on the calendar twice.

reading: March is around the corner, and with it, your birthday on the equinox. The Sagittarius moon is already planning a party. You will feel restless and hopeful today, like someone who just spotted the first robin of spring, even though there is still a foot of snow outside.

Use that energy to plan something fun for next month, something that has nothing to do with work. A day trip, a new skill, a small adventure. The [[Knight of Wands]] says one adventure, not twelve. Pick it, name it, and put it on the calendar in red.
joel.mission: Plan one fun thing for March today and write it on your calendar in red ink.
joel.omen: An arrow drawn in the snow or painted on a wall. Your next adventure is pointing straight at you.
joel.stoneWhy: steady aim for the archer
joel.elementWhy: Sagittarius is a fire sign too

reading: The archer moon is optimistic, and some of that optimism is about to land in your lap. You will hear good news today, small but warm, like a letter from an old friend or a plan that finally comes together.

In the afternoon, you will feel like going somewhere. Maybe the shore, to look at the ice along the water's edge. Maybe just around the block. Go. The [[Six of Swords]] is sailing on, and today the water is a little clearer, a little closer to the other side. Spring is out there.
nancy.mission: Go for a short walk today with no destination in mind and see where the arrow takes you.
nancy.omen: A bird flying north overhead. It means spring is sending scouts.
nancy.stoneWhy: bright and clear for good news

together.text: Each of you suggests one small adventure the other should try in March. Something new but doable: a different walk, a new song, a strange museum. Accept the dare without negotiation. The archer is already aiming, and it never misses a friend.

title: February Takes Its Final Bow
skyStory: On the last night of February, the moon sits at forty-six percent in Sagittarius, half lit and grinning like it just finished a good book. The shortest month bows gracefully, gathers its scarves, and steps off stage. March is waiting in the wings, impatient, carrying a birthday cake with a single candle shaped like a tiger.

reading: The month is closing, and it is a good time to look back. What did you finish? What did you start? What did you let someone else carry for once? Make a short list. It will be longer than you think.

Then turn your face toward March. Your birthday is coming, the equinox, the moment day and night stand perfectly level. The Tiger is about to start a whole new year of its own. Tonight, give yourself one small gift: an evening with no tasks at all. The [[Nine of Cups]] wants you to feel full, not finished.
joel.mission: Write a list of three good things that happened in February and read it aloud to the cabin.
joel.omen: A calendar page turning in a breeze. It means a fresh start is arriving right on time.
joel.stoneWhy: warm red for the month's end

reading: February was short, but you filled it. Stories told, people helped, small victories quietly stacked one on top of the other. The Wood Rat counts them all tonight, in a cozy corner, and is pleased with the total.

Tomorrow is March, and with it comes a certain birthday you will want to plan for. You will feel the itch already. Good. But tonight, rest. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] reminds you that joy does not have to be earned before it is allowed. Let it in. Let February go, scarves and all.
nancy.mission: Tell someone the best story from your February, with your hands doing at least half the work.
nancy.omen: The first evening you notice the sun setting later. It means the light is returning, just as you always do.
nancy.stoneWhy: a month of small wins, stacked

together.text: Send each other one favourite moment from February, whether that was a typo, a blue jay or two orange shovels. Then say goodbye to the month together, out loud, at the same minute. March is knocking, and it is bringing a birthday.
